items.title: Meituan releases LongCat-2.5 weights under MIT, 1.6T total and ~48B active, multimodal
items.summary: Meituan published the weights for its natively multimodal agentic model LongCat-2.5 (1.6T parameters, about 48B active) under an MIT license, a week after announcing it. Builders can now self-host or fine-tune a large open agentic-coding and visual-coding model.

reception.summary: Replies were mostly praise for the MIT license; one user asked for a tested hardware and quantization table because 48B active does not mean it fits like a 48B model, and one said they enjoyed using it in Hermes. Benchmarks and self-hosting reports were not out yet.

items.title: NaceAI says Drex Max v1.1 tops Artificial Analysis Decision Index, open weights promised
items.summary: NaceAI reports its Drex Max v1.1 decision model ranks first on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index and is available through an API with about 1M free requests, with a technical report on arXiv. Weights are described as coming soon, not released.

items.title: AutoRLBench tests whether agents can find the root cause of failed RL training runs
items.summary: OpenBMB released a benchmark built from real failed RL runs (configs, logs, metrics intact, no synthetic bugs) and scored 10 frontier agents; the best reaches about 40%, and agents do worse on implicit data bugs than config bugs.

items.title: InferenceBench trend: frontier models' inference speed-up factor grew from 3x to 12x
items.summary: Maksym Andriushchenko posted the historical trend on InferenceBench (Sep 2025 to Oct 2026): the speed-up frontier models achieve on the benchmark rose from 3x to 12x, with a doubling time of about 6.3 months. Results are published at inferencebench.ai.
